video_title: Understanding Transformer Attention Mechanisms & Positional Encodings

segments.text: Welcome to today's lecture on sequence-to-sequence models and the revolutionary Transformer architecture introduced by Vaswani et al in 2017.
Before Transformers, recurrent neural networks and LSTMs processed tokens sequentially, creating an information bottleneck and preventing parallelization across long sequences.
Scaled Dot-Product Attention computes attention weights using Query, Key, and Value matrices. The formula divides the dot product of Q and K transpose by the square root of dk.
Multi-Head Attention projects Queries, Keys, and Values h times with different learned linear projections, allowing the model to jointly attend to information at different representation subspaces.
Since the Transformer contains no recurrence and no convolution, positional encodings using sinusoidal functions of different frequencies are added to input embeddings to inject sequence order.
Layer normalization and residual connections wrap around both multi-head attention and position-wise feed-forward networks to stabilize gradients during deep network optimization.
The decoder stack incorporates masked multi-head attention, which prevents positions from attending to subsequent future tokens during autoregressive language generation.
Cross-attention in the decoder allows query vectors from the decoder self-attention layer to attend over key and value vectors produced by the final encoder layer.

benchmark_queries.query: What is the formula for Scaled Dot-Product Attention?
Why did recurrent neural networks create an information bottleneck?
How do multi-head attention layers capture different representation subspaces?
How does the Transformer inject sequence order without recurrence?
What prevents the decoder from looking ahead at future tokens?
Where do the query and key vectors originate in cross-attention?
